prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor plaza with a large church facade receding into the background (8–25 m away above and behind the crowd) and a cluster of people standing on paved ground that slopes upward from the bottom edge. In frame 1, the camera wearer looks upward so people's heads and a blue umbrella appear near the bottom at roughly 1.5–4 m, while across frames 2 to 5 the view tilts downward and the camera wearer moves closer to two women in the center-left foreground (in a white top and a blue denim jacket, facing away and to the right) who become bright white at 0.5–1.0 m—within arm's reach of the camera wearer and less than 0.5 m from each other. A semi-circle of four men on the right (in a dark jacket, black hoodie, green jacket, and maroon top, facing roughly toward the group and partially toward the camera wearer) stands at mid-range gray values of about 1.5–3.5 m, spaced 0.5–1.0 m apart, while a man in a burgundy jacket stands further back at 3–4 m beneath the umbrella (about 1 m above him) and distant vendor carts on the left sit at 8–15 m. Across the five frames, the foreground woman in white increasingly occludes the people and umbrella behind her, while the person in maroon on the far right remains partly cropped by the right frame edge and holds a small object within their own arm's reach. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous ground-plane gradient and the clear metric separation between the immediate foreground pair, the mid-ground semi-circle of men, and the receding church wall immediately apparent, though it is unreliable on the sky and distant plaza buildings (which collapse to uniform black) and flattens fine details like held cups and faces into uniform silhouettes.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete people, umbrellas, a handbag strap, and a held cup ('bowl') as colored masks against an unsegmented black background representing the plaza pavement, church, and sky. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera tilts down and approaches the group, the pink/brown mask of the woman in white (0.5–1.0 m directly in front, facing away) and the purple/light-blue mask of the woman in the denim jacket (1.0–1.5 m to the left, facing right) expand to fill the lower center and left, placing both women within arm's reach of the camera wearer and directly adjacent to each other. To their right, three to four men stand 1.5–3.5 m away and 0.5–1.0 m apart facing left and toward the camera wearer, while behind and above the foreground women at 3–4 m are a man in burgundy beneath a large blue umbrella and distant left-side pedestrians and vendor umbrellas at 8–15 m. The masks clearly track occlusions over time, showing the foreground women progressively blocking the man in burgundy, the umbrella canopy above them, and the mid-ground men, while figures at the bottom and right edges remain partially out of view. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to count overlapping individuals in the dense crowd and spot small held or worn items within arm's reach of the women—such as the green cup labeled 'bowl' in frame 2 and the diagonal 'handbag' strap in frame 3—but it is unreliable across time because the cup and strap are missed in most frames, far-background buildings disappear completely, and in frame 5 the woman in white's hair and cup merge with the person behind her while labels overlap.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across frames 1 to 4, failing to detect any body or hand keypoints despite the crowd of people standing 0.5–15 m away in the plaza. Only in frame 5 does a single magenta hand skeleton appear in the upper-left-center region, corresponding to the raised left hand of the foreground woman in the white shirt who stands about 0.6 m in front of the camera wearer—well within the camera wearer's arm's reach—with her back turned and head angled slightly left. This detected hand is positioned just to the left of her head and in front of the woman in the denim jacket (about 1 m away on the left) and the man in burgundy (about 3 m behind), with fingers curled around the small green cup within her own arm's reach while her torso occludes the people behind her. In frame 5, the magenta wireframe makes the exact finger articulation and grip orientation around the cup clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB image alone. However, the map is overwhelmingly unreliable for spatial layout, distance, facing direction, or multi-person tracking, as it misses every yellow body skeleton across all five frames and fails to detect the other visible hands holding food or cups in frames 2 through 5.
